reasons: Both answers meet every rubric item. A's error is in its advice: it says math.fsum([0.1, 0.2]) == 0.3 is True, which suggests fsum fixes the comparison problem when it does not. B's errors are only in illustrative outputs, and B adds useful guidance on exact alternatives (Decimal/Fraction), DB column types and JSON serialization of prices.

A: Claims math.fsum([0.1, 0.2]) == 0.3 is True; a two-operand IEEE addition is already correctly rounded, so fsum returns 0.30000000000000004 and the comparison is False.
B: Claims sum([0.1] * 1_000_000) gives 100.00000000001164 and the Decimal sum is 100.00; a million 0.1s sum to about 100000 (float gives ~100000.0000013329).
